summary: Read-only two-project integration brief: (1) annunimas-human-tenant provides Obsidian-compatible human knowledge-graph scanning and links notes to persistent-memory contracts (src/lib.rs:1-6, src/lib.rs:92-150). Concrete risk: MemoryStore::store serializes records but discards the result, so scans do not actually persist memory (src/lib.rs:56-89). (2) the upstream Annunimas core/Mnemosyne project supplies the memory contract and intended persistence layer consumed through direct path dependencies (Cargo.toml:12-20; docs/migration-notes.md:3-10). Concrete risk: tenant operation remains coupled to the upstream repository layout and an unfinished compatibility seam (docs/migration-notes.md:9-10). Shared autonomous-agent safety boundary: human material is private and untrusted until classified; agents must distinguish raw, generated, human, governance, and runtime authority, must not silently promote or overwrite human material, and must escalate unresolved conflicts for review rather than guess (docs/human-knowledge-ingestion-contract.md:21-25,49-69,96-114,145-152). Actionable recommendation: introduce the planned tenant-facing memory adapter, replace direct Annunimas path dependencies with that boundary, and make persistence preserve provenance, authority, status, privacy, and review-required metadata before any agent can rely on ingested notes (docs/migration-notes.md:9; docs/human-knowledge-ingestion-contract.md:71-94,115-123). Declared clean-tree check passed exactly as specified; no files were modified.
